svg.text: Union accounting system (1971, Varian 620/f): two boundaries between applications and a hand-written supervisor
Applications
loaded into an overlay area, run until the terminal
buffer is full, swapped out
Supervisor
preemptive; manages interrupts and IO; dribbles
characters out at 30 cps
30-cps terminals
applications never know what device their output
goes to
Boundary 1: character output (dependency normal) applications pass strings to the
supervisor; compile-time dependencies point with the flow of control, hiding the
device
Boundary 2: dependency inverted the supervisor starts every application by jumping
to the same address in the overlay area, a polymorphic interface with no compile-
time dependency on them
4-TEL: splitting the COLT and the SAC
30 cps was too slow, so analysis and reports moved to the service area computer
(SAC) while the COLT only dials and measures; short DSL packets like DIAL XXXX or
MEASURE cross a clean, decoupled boundary
Vectorization: chips as plugins
30 EPROMs held one 30K binary, so any change meant replacing all of them; fix: 32
source files under 1K, a 40-byte address table per chip, all calls indirect via RAM
vectors: independently deployable chips, polymorphic dispatch, a literal plugin
architecture, and patching by dial-up
